title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
abstract: arXiv:2611.16097v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study smooth calibration error in sequential binary prediction, a measure of how far probabilistic forecasts are from being calibrated that is robust to small perturbations of the forecasts. The minimax smooth calibration error is known to lie between $\Omega(T^{1/3})$ and $O(\sqrt T)$(Qiao and Zheng, 2024), where $T$ is the number of rounds. We close this gap for both adaptive and oblivious adversaries. We construct an adaptive adversary whose outcome mean moves with the forecaster's cumulative residual, which makes compensating for past residuals costly and forces every forecaster to incur $\Omega(\sqrt T)$ expected smooth calibration error. Simulating this adversary against the forecaster's average prediction yields an oblivious adversary with the same guarantee. tldr: 本文通过构造自适应对手和遗忘对手，证明在线平滑校准误差的极小极大下界为 Ω(√T)，填补了已知的上下界差距，确立了平滑校准误差的极小极大最优性。
en_tdlr: This paper closes the gap between known bounds on the minimax smooth calibration error by constructing adaptive and oblivious adversaries that force every forecaster to incur Ω(√T) expected smooth calibration error, matching the known O(√T) upper bound and establishing minimax optimality.
